messages:
maya: Heads up — getting reports of partial traces for /api/search from a big customer. Trace tree shows frontend + aggregator only, backend spans (cache/payment) missing. Started ~2028-07-20 15:10 UTC.
tracing-oncall: Incident created: #INC-4782 — triage in eng-platform. Pinged @leo @anika.
leo: can you paste a sample trace id and region?
maya: trace id: 4fa2b9c3e8d14f7b (customer-prod-us-east). I can reproduce locally by piping that id into the prod stream.
ingest-bot: exporter_queue_depth prod-otlp spiked to 96% at 2028-07-20T15:12:02Z :warning:
anika: looking at otel-collector canary logs — seeing repeated warnings: "attribute value length exceeded, truncating" then errors: "span dropped: invalid attributes". snippets:
```
2028-07-20T15:11:58Z collector[otlp] WARN attributes_processor: dropped attribute \"http.route\" (len=768) — max=256
2028-07-20T15:11:58Z exporter[otlp] ERROR exporter.go: failed to export batch: span validation failed, rejecting 42 spans
```
sam: that prod-canary pushed a new sanitizer config that changed max_attr_len from 1024 -> 256 for perf; looks like we accidentally deployed a variant with it set to 64 in prod-canary.
leo: truncation explains validation errors, but dropped spans should still show up partially. Why are spans completely absent?
anika: digging deeper — tempo/jaeger retention TTL job runs every 5m. collector is stamping spans with timestamps about +1 hour in the future because the sanitizer changed timezone handling when normalizing attributes. With backend TTL cutoff <1h those future-stamped spans get treated as "too old" and are purged immediately.
maya: so two simultaneous failures: aggressive attribute truncation causing validation rejects, and timestamp skew causing immediate TTL deletes. :scream: 
tracing-oncall: recommendation: rollback prod-canary otel-collector. Who can coordinate?
leo: rolling back otel-collector in prod-canary now: `kubectl -n telemetry rollout undo deploy/otel-collector --to-revision=12`
sam: pushing hotfix to sanitizer: bump max_attr_len to 512 and revert the timezone/timestamp change. PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/telemetry/commit/ae2f8
ingest-bot: exporter_queue_depth prod-otlp back to 14% after rollback at 2028-07-20T15:18:23Z :thumbsup:
anika: confirmed we can now fetch spans for trace 4fa2b9c3e8d14f7b from tempo: `curl -s \"http://tempo.prod/internal/traces/4fa2b9c3e8d14f7b\" | jq .spans | length` -> 18
maya: customer verified full traces visible in their dashboard, no regressions for last 30m. Forwarding to CS.
leo: follow-ups: 1) add e2e test that generates long attributes and asserts collector doesn't drop spans, 2) alert for exporter_queue_depth and a metric for immediate-ttl-deletes, 3) add a canary gate to block config flips that change timestamp handling.
sam: opened follow-up issues: #TELEM-213 (sanitize e2e) and #TELEM-214 (ttl-monitor). Will add unit tests and run an extended staging canary.
maya: thanks all — I'll update the incident ticket with timeline and schedule the postmortem.
tracing-oncall: Incident resolved — moving to postmortem pending write-up. :white_check_mark:
